newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DUNFERMLINE OUT OF SCOTTISH CUP, RANGERS MARCH ON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUNFERMLINE OUT OF SCOTTISH CUP, RANGERS MARCH ON.

text.p: Premier division Dunfermline were knocked out of the Scottish Cup in the fourth round on Saturday, going down 2-1 at first division Falkirk, but league leaders Rangers made no mistake against the team with the worst record, beating East Fife 3-0 at Ibrox.
Stewart Petrie put Dunfermline ahead in the 12th minute but Kevin McAllister levelled in the 27th.
Dunfermline dominated the game but David Hagen escaped to hit the winner 18 minutes from time.
There was no fairy tale for East Fife, however. They had managed just one league win in the first division this season before taking on the cream of Scottish soccer.
David Robertson put the champions ahead early and Trevor Steven made it 2-0 after 28 minutes.
Ally McCoist hit the third in the 37th but the expected goal glut failed to materialise and East Fife can go home with their pride intact after a brave second-half show.
Premier division strugglers Motherwell were held to a 1-1 home draw by second division Hamilton as the visitors' Guy Clarke cancelled out Owen Coyle's first-half opener.

Raith had a scare, going behind to second division Brechin, but came through 2-1 with second-half goals by Steve Kirk and Soeren Andersen while Kilmarnock edged Clyde 1-0 away with a second-half Paul Wright penalty.
In an all-first division game Greenock Morton and Dundee drew 2-2.
Hearts are at home to fellow premier division Dundee United on Sunday in the top game of the weekend.
